To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the positive predictive value of predicting hyperkalemias induced by DDIs is low, but that continuous monitoring of the current potassium level shows better predictive power than predicting at the time of drug order.

continuous monitoring of the risk to develop hyperkalemia by taking into account the current serum potassium level shows better predictive power than prediction triggered at the onset and taking into account more parameters at this time.

the predictive power of DDI alerts can be significantly improved by continuous monitoring of the risk of hyperkalemias, whereas adding further patient parameters at the onset of DDIs does not significantly improve prediction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing strategies for predicting hyper- and hypokalemia in potassium- and magnesium-increasing DDIs, respectively.
the question of how to best improve the prediction of hyperkalemias induced by potassium-increasing DDIns.
the prediction of hyperkalemias in hospitalized patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
continuous monitoring of potassium-increasing DDs is superior to predictions triggered at the start of DDIs.
a combination of continuous monitoring and the consideration of additional patient parameters at the onset of DDIs is the best strategy for predicting hyperkalmia in hospitalized patients.
continuous monitoring of potassium levels is the most reliable strategy to predict hyperkalemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
continuous monitoring is the most powerful strategy to predict hyperkalemia.
continuous monitoring of the serum potassium level is superior to the prediction of hyperkalemias based on the current patient parameters at the onset of the DDI.
the best prediction of hyperkalemias due to DDI is obtained by continuous monitoring of the current potassium level and patient-specific parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the predictive power of the risk for drug-induced hyperkalemia is not significantly improved by taking into account additional patient parameters.
the predictive power of DDI alerts can be improved by continuous monitoring.
the best strategy for predicting hyperkolemia in DDIs is to monitor patients’ potassium levels continuously.
